$description: Semantic layer. Every token here is a decision, expressed as a reference to a base primitive. The one declared exception is shadow geometry (offset, blur, spread), whose single home is this file. Re-point a base primitive and the whole system re-tones without a component being touched.

heading.$description: h1 to h3. One real tonal step above body.

body.$description: Running text and the surfaces it sits between.

quote-on-dark.$description: Quoted text on a permanently dark ground. The dark theme context already re-points text.quote to this value inside the dark scope; this token is for the surfaces that are dark whatever the theme is — glass on an ink scrim, a card on the spec heroes' gradient — which cannot reach that context and would otherwise take the light value. Same role, stated for the case the context does not cover.

quote.$description: Quoted text. The same colour as secondary in light; the dark theme context gives it its own step (white at 78%) so a pull quote reads as quieter than body without going grey on ink.

disabled.$description: Held back on a white ground: the disabled sidebar row, the Documentation separator, the eyebrow's unreachable trail — and the scrollbar's resting thumb, which is the same idea (present, not asking for attention). The dark counterpart is text.disabled-on-dark. 25% rather than the 14% the bar first used: on white, ink below about a fifth simply is not there.

disabled-on-dark.$description: The same role on an ink ground — a step of ink's own light. Bound by component.sidebar.fg-disabled, which is what the surfaces read.

heading-on-dark.$description: Heading text on an ink ground. The dark-theme counterpart of text.heading, bound by the --port-text-heading alias under [data-theme=dark].

body-on-dark.$description: Running text on an ink ground. The dark-theme counterpart of text.body.

secondary-on-dark.$description: Muted and meta on an ink ground (#99a1af). The dark-theme counterpart of text.secondary.

brand-on-ink.$description: Brand blue for text on an ink ground. NOT named -on-dark, and the suffix is the whole point: -on-dark means the base name re-points to this one inside the dark scope, which CV1 and the C clauses both rely on. text.brand cannot do that, because it names two roles at once — link text, and the fill that text.on-brand sits on. Re-pointing it lifted the fill too and put white on a light blue at 2.57:1, which CV1 caught. So this is a sibling role rather than a twin: a surface binds it directly where its ground is ink, C15 measures it there, and text.brand keeps its value in both themes.

status.$description: Status badges (the term sheet's Status fact). One tone per state; only shipped exists so far. A green fill, green text, and a green ring, all reading on either card ground.

shipped-bg.$description: Green highlight fill for a Shipped status.

shipped-fg.$description: Green text on the shipped fill over a light ground.

shipped-fg-on-dark.$description: Green text on the shipped fill over an ink ground. The dark-theme counterpart of shipped-fg, reached by the --port-status-shipped-fg alias.

background.$description:
THE ELEVATION LADDER, stated so it is a model rather than a habit.

Level 0 is the page itself: `page` in light, re-pointed to `ink` by the dark theme context. Level 1 is a thing lying ON the page — a card, a popover, a menu — and is `card` / `card-on-dark`, each one step of the ground's own light composited into an opaque colour so it can be handed to a third party that has nowhere to layer a translucent fill. `utility` is not a rung: it is the top bar's own ground on a light page, a sibling of level 0 rather than a step above it.

There is no level 2, and that is a statement of fact rather than an omission: nothing in this surface nests a panel inside a panel. A third rung would be `background.level-2` plus its surface, built the same way — one more step of the ground's light through the build's `over` composite — and it is not declared until something renders it, because a token with no client is drift the gate counts (H1). KERN carries level-1 and level-2 because government forms nest; this surface does not, yet.

card.$description: Elevated card, popover and menu surface on the white page. The mirror of background.card-on-dark: that one is ink's light at 6.25% resolved onto ink, this one is ink at 6.25% resolved onto white. Opaque for the same reason — it is handed to fumadocs as a single popover colour, and a translucent popover shows the page through it. It used to be pure white, which left an elevated surface indistinguishable from the ground it sat on.

card-on-dark.$description: Elevated card surface on an ink ground — one step lighter than the page, per the dark-mode base/elevated split (Apple HIG). The dark-theme counterpart of background.card. A step of ink's own light composited onto ink, so it follows ink without being a second dark hex. Opaque on purpose: this is also the docs popover and menu fill (app/ame/ame.css hands it to fumadocs as one value), and a translucent popover shows the page through it.

ink.$description: Dark surfaces: mark card, splash, iPhone card.

utility.$description: Top utility bar on a light ground. On dark the bar is ink (background.ink) so it blends into the page; see component.topbar.bg-on-dark.

hairline-on-dark.$description: Every rule and ring on an ink ground: card edges, the divider under the expertise grid, the carousel arrows' rings, the endorsement and Resume button outlines. The same step of ink's own light the held-back rows take (component.sidebar.fg-disabled), so a line and a disabled label read at one weight instead of two. It replaced a color-mix of the live text colour at 18%, which was a value nothing else in the system shared.

surface.$description: The glass system. Tint and pole are the ground; the fg pair is the foreground the glass carries, declared once per backdrop tone. Which of the two pairs is live is a runtime state, switched by [data-backdrop] in portfolio.css; the values are decided here.

btn-secondary.$description: Secondary (dark) button fill; the -30 variant is this at 30% via color-mix in portfolio.css. A step of ink's own light over the ink page.

btn-secondary-edge.$description: Secondary (dark) button edge: the top of the lift ramp, so the hairline reads as the same light the fill carries, further up.

glass-fg-on-light.$description: Glass foreground over a light backdrop.

glass-fg-on-dark.$description: Glass foreground over a dark backdrop.

glass-fill-on-light.$description: Glass background over a light backdrop.

glass-fill-on-dark.$description: Glass background over a dark backdrop.

card-glass.$description: The work card's ground on a light page — ink at 2%, the exact inverse of the 2% of ink's light the dark card lifts with (component.card.background-lift-on-dark). It was white at 70%, which over a white page resolved to very nearly the page itself: a card with no edge and no lift.

glass-fill-opaque-on-light-ground.$description: The white backing under the opaque light glass. Coverage, not colour — the mirror of surface.glass-fill-opaque-on-dark-ground, and it keeps the panel solid over content while its backdrop-filter is suppressed mid-transform.

glass-fill-opaque-on-light.$description: The opaque glass variant over a light backdrop: modals that must stay solid over content. The tone only — ink at 11%, mirroring the 11% of ink's light the dark panel carries; the coverage beneath it is glass-fill-opaque-on-light-ground.

glass-fill-opaque-on-dark-ground.$description: The ink backing under the opaque dark glass. Coverage, not colour: it is what keeps the panel solid over content while its backdrop-filter is suppressed mid-transform. surface.glass-fill-opaque-on-dark is the light that rides on top of it.

glass-fill-opaque-on-dark.$description: The opaque glass variant over a dark backdrop. Shared by the cookie, contact, and Ask-AI panels. A step of ink's own light, so the panel reads as a layer above the dark card rather than a hole in it — the job the old lab() hex did, now on the ramp.

dither-tile.$description: Repeat size of the grain tile on every dithered surface.

bg.$description: Glass nav base tint, and the selection pill's fill.

bg-on-dark.$description: The selection pill over a dark backdrop: brighter, not darker, because the selected label stays dark.

type.$description: Typographic roles. Size, leading, tracking, and weight synthesis composed from the base scale.

control-size.$description: Text size for interactive chrome: buttons, pills, menu rows, inline controls. Not for prose — see body-size. Rationale: decisions.md D-52.

loose-leading.$description: Comfortable leading for running prose: lead paragraphs, centred intros, pull quotes, muted body. For continuous reading, not headings — see docs-title-leading. Rationale: decisions.md D-50.

meta-leading.$description: Leading for meta text, paired with meta-size. Use wherever meta-size is bound. Rationale: decisions.md D-50.

tight-tracking.$description: Tight tracking for UI controls and headings, at any size. Not hero-specific — see hero-tracking for the hero line itself. Rationale: decisions.md D-50.

docs-title-leading.$description: Line-height for the docs page title (the h1 under .ame-docs-root: case-study and /ame pages). The body/paragraph leading ratio (1.6, font.leading.loose) rather than the tight hero leading, so a wrapped title breathes like the running text does, proportionate to its larger size. Read by app/ame/ame.css.

heading-synthesis.$description: The live header weight synthesis. Every h1 to h3 on the surface is a stroked 400, not a 460 cut.

body-leading.$description: Line-height for running body copy set in a measure-limited column. dense-leading is the tighter role for stacked rows; this is the one a paragraph reads.

body-synthesis.$description: The live body weight synthesis, set on .portfolio-root.

icon-stroke.$description: Lucide icon stroke width, 1.5. The .lucide default rule in portfolio.css reads var(--type-icon-stroke) so every icon is 1.5 without a per-icon prop.

dense-leading.$description: Line-height for dense rows: the footer's stacked links and meta lines.

font-body.$description: The face the running text is set in. A surface binds this rather than font.family.sans, so a docs area that wants a different face re-points one semantic name instead of reaching into the base tier for the family list.

nav-synthesis.$description: The synthesized stroke on the glass nav. The same 460 the headings take today, named separately because a nav is not a heading: if either moves, the other should not have to.

sidebar-label-size.$description: The docs sidebar smallest supporting text: group separators, the disabled shortcut row. Two steps below the row size, so a label reads as a label for the group rather than a sibling of the entries under it.

space.$description: Brand spacing decisions from the unit ramp.

stack-relaxed.$description: Heading to body on a reference page: the stack, three ramp steps up from the 1rem the prose default uses. Reference pages are tables and figures rather than running text, and the shared rhythm reads tight when almost every block has its own top edge. Exists because a surface may not bind unit.7 directly -- U1 caught exactly that, which is the rule doing its job on the person who wrote it.

motion.$description: Motion by role. Components reach for these, not raw durations or curves.

squish-duration.$description: The segmented-pill squish bounce (nav, 3D/2D toggle, accessibility Segmented).

card-duration.$description: The card hover transition (.port-card box-shadow + transform), 220ms.

enter-duration.$description: Entrance fades: the work-card enter animation and the case-study stagger, 520ms (snapped from 0.5s/0.6s onto the scale).

exit-ease.$description: Mobile menu and contact sheet close.

elevation.$description: Shadow recipes. Every colour is the ink at a graded alpha, referenced, so the whole shadow system re-tones from one primitive. Offset, blur, and spread are declared here: this file is their single home.

glass-edge.$description: The glass border, on its own so a surface can pick its strength without touching its drop. Every .port-glass surface carries one of these: the AI panel, the cookie modal, the nav, the top bar, the contact sheets. The default was doubled from 0.06 to 0.12 on 2026-07-29 so the edge reads against the page (D-23).

glass-edge-light.$description: The faint edge, for a surface that should stay quiet. The nav takes this one: it sits high on the page against plain paper, where the full edge reads as a hard outline.

glass-edge-on-dark.$description: The default edge over a dark backdrop. Doubled from 0.10 to 0.20 alongside the light tone, so both read at the same strength (D-23).

glass-edge-light-on-dark.$description: The faint edge over a dark backdrop.

glass-drop.$description: The glass drop, paired with any edge above.

pill-on-dark.$description: The nav pill over a dark backdrop: a slightly stronger edge and a deeper drop, because it sits on an opaque light fill against dark glass.

state.$description: Interaction states, named for what they mean rather than for the value they take. KERN keeps a family of these; ame had none, and the consequence was measurable: disabled was rendered at 0.70, 0.40, 25% and 10.7% in four different places, none of them wrong on its own and no two agreeing.

opacity-disabled.$description: The opacity a disabled control takes. A surface binds this rather than a Tailwind opacity-40 class, so the four values collapse to one and moving it moves them together.

focus.$description: The focus ring. The same hue the brand takes today, named for focus because a focus indicator is an accessibility obligation (WCAG 2.4.11/2.4.13) and must be able to move without dragging the brand with it.

opacity-hover.$description: The opacity a filled control takes under the pointer. Named alongside opacity-disabled so the two hover/disabled treatments move together rather than being invented per surface.
